messages:
maya: heads-up — brought a new reranker (ranky4b-v2) into shadowbench using passage-level candidates vs our usual chunked 512-token passages. seeing weird NDCG/MRR split.

alex: what do you mean by split? numbers?

maya: overall NDCG@10 down 1.8% relative to baseline, MRR@1 up 2.2%. per-slice it's worse for short queries. full run: eval-bot posted summary:

eval-bot: run: ranky4b-v2 | candidateization: passage vs chunked
- NDCG@10: baseline_chunked=0.421, passage=0.413
- MRR@1: baseline_chunked=0.291, passage=0.297
- short-query slice (len<=5): NDCG@10 drop -3.5% ; MRR@1 +1.0%
- long-query slice (len>20): NDCG@10 no change; MRR slight win

lee: interesting. could be candidate ordering — passage candidates preserve sentence boundaries, chunking breaks them and inflates negative examples.

noah: also check overlap with anchor-set. chunking increases near-duplicate candidates which may change inter-doc contrast.

maya: good point. i reused the same candidate pool size (k=100) for both. command I ran:

```
python eval.py --model ranky4b-v2 --candidates chunked --k 100 --holdout release_A
python eval.py --model ranky4b-v2 --candidates passage --k 100 --holdout release_A
```

maya: attaching quick sample where passage beats chunked for short queries:

- Q: "reset password" (short)
  - passage top: doc A (ndcg contrib 0.35) — direct match
  - chunked top: doc B (ndcg contrib 0.12) — partial sentence match

alex: can you dump candidate text examples and tokenization? maybe whitespace/newline boundaries are altering embeddings/priming.

maya: uploading short dump to /s3/evals/chunk-v-passages/6630004321-samples.csv : s3://redwood-evals/6630004321-samples.csv

lee: suggestion: run controlled ablation: keep candidate text identical but vary chunk offsets vs sentence-preserving split. also try k=20 to see head effect.

noah: also try normalizing punctuation and trimming leading/trailing fragments; sometimes chunking leaves half-sentences that confuse rerankers.

alex: FYI quantized run earlier? did we use int8 for ranky4b-v2 in this bench?

maya: this was FP16. we also have a quantized int8 shadow run scheduled next week — will add both chunked & passage there.

maya: action items:
- maya: run candidate-level parity dump + tokenization (today)
- maya: ablation with k=20 and sentence-preserving chunks (tomorrow)
- lee: check anchor-set overlap and near-duplicate rate (EOD)
- noah: add normalization step (trim/fragments) to preprocess (tomorrow)

alex: thanks — ping me when dumps are up. might be a model scoring bias rather than true relevance regression.

maya: will do. :thumbsup:
